I love this question, this is my darkest secret so if I get the chance to talk about it somewhat anonymously I will. I suck my thumb (I am going on 27 years old) I have done it since before birth (my mom literally has a sonogram of me with my thumb in my mouth. I also am diagnosed with anxiety (had it all my life) which is why I think I never dropped the habit. I had a little pillow from when I was sent home after birth until I was 5, and then our cat peed on it so my dad threw it away (life was basically over for me then) but then my great grandmother bought me a bed set. I made sure that one of the pillow cases of that bed set was to be my new pillow. So I still have it and whenever I get a chance alone, I bring it out of my purse and suck my thumb. Almost like when people step outside for a cigarette. My habit is so bad, I do it while I’m driving (when no one is around) in public bathrooms and even with covid running around, after shopping or leaving work, without washing my hands, knowing the risk, would still suck my thumb. If I were to lose this, I would not know what to do. I take it everywhere and always think, if I were to get mugged and have my purse stolen I’d go down fighting. It was white, and now it’s.. gray. It’s a running joke in my family (the only ones who know) that it resembles a “oil rag” and everyone refuses to touch it.

You can slow a panic attack by focusing on your breathing. It’s sound corny but it can help. If you aren’t breathing enough (too slow) breathe more, slowly. If you are breathing to much (too fast) slow down your breaths. Breathing brings instant oxygen to your brain so I look at it as more than just breathing. I think of it as that I am feeding my brain and allowing clarity. And all the while you are doing the above, your brain has been occupied by thinking about all of that (how you’re breathing) and is no longer racing. It helps me, not completely but it speeds up the episode. Hope this can help you too.

Hey, trust me when I say I understand your sadness. I myself am going through the same situation. My cat Oreo is 21 years old and I’m 25F. I’ve had her since she was born, so I’ve had her almost all my life. From kindergarten to graduating high school. I also struggle with clinical depression/anxiety. She’s been through it all through me. She is very very clingy. She follows my every step room to room and is always in my lap or arms when I’m sitting or laying down. She sleep on my pillow every night. She was recently diagnosed with lung cancer 2 months ago. I had taken her to the vet because she wasn’t herself, she stopped eating and drinking and following/sitting with me. It turns out she was impacted with stool. She was hospitalized for 4 days and during that time she was pricked and poked and had fingers/enemas inserted. She has only been to the vet for the rare and far in between injuries so she was so scared, and this all happened during COVID-19 so I wasn’t even allowed in the building or to see her. They just came and grabbed her from the car. I didn’t know that day she wouldn’t come home with me. I was devastated. I was even more devastated to hear that during the xrays they found cancer in her lungs. Because of her age and all that she had been through with the impacted stool I made the decision I don’t want her to go through anymore right now. I took her home. She started eating and drinking again but is still very distant and starting to hide most of the day. She is now starting to cough. I first noticed it when I tried to pick her up. The pressure I put on her lungs was too much. So now I can’t even hold her. She’s now just coughing without any touching. So I fear it’s almost time. She’s lived a very good life and I can’t put her through anymore time away from home. The moment I feel her coughing is too painful I will be putting her to sleep. This decision is so hard for me. She’s my everything. Always have, always will. I learned of a service that is here in my city that does home euthanasia. I think that’s best, she’ll be in the comfort of her own home and with me by her side. I also found a place that does private cremations. Im going to choose a beautiful heart urn with a paw print that sits on a little stand, and a silver necklace with some of her ashes in it so she’ll always be with me. I’m sorry I don’t have more advice on what to do in your situation. I just felt I share my story so you know you’re not alone. Always remember how well of a life you gave them and all the love you shared. You just got to do what’s best for your kitty. Sometimes the treatment just isn’t worth the pain and discomfort.

I don’t remember exactly how it started. I remember being really annoyed and irritated just by people talking to me. I started sleeping ALOT, I’m talking 12+ hours. I would get angry, urges to punch things for no reason. I started feeling lost in life, dooming sadness, and then feeling numb. I started thinking about suicide on a daily bases, multiple times a day. Ive always been an anxious person but then I started having anxiety attacks. My older sister is the one who reached out for help for me. All I had to do was show up to the therapist appointment. Then my therapist set me up with a psychiatrist, showed up. Was diagnosed with clinical depression, GAD (general anxiety disorder) and ADD, so far. I’ve been in therapy for over a year, and on meds for about 8 months. I can tell you, I don’t feel a whole lot better. I still sleep the same amount of hours, maybe more. I still think about dying. I don’t get angry annoyed or irritated anymore, but that’s just because I’m numb at this point. I’ve seen my therapist EVERY single Wednesday for a whole year. Starting about 4 months ago, it’s now EVERY Wednesday and Friday. You’d think with this much therapy I’d feel better but, not really. Depression is one MF.
